author: blu
body: Do NOT restore a binary search here. This was one until 2026-07-28 (main 11369) and it silently found only some of its names: a binary search requires the list to be ordered by the comparison it searches with, and the list is written alphabetically while text-compare orders by CCE, which numbers letters by frequency. `i` is 19 and `c` is 24, so `int-mod` sorts before `char-at` under the comparator and after it in the list. Names past the first inversion were unreachable, and an unreachable builtin does not fail loudly -- it falls through to the ordinary apply path and emits a call to a function the target language has never heard of. Measured per plug by codex/plugs/test-input/builtin-reach.codex, a probe that cites nothing so its calls reach this table. Thirteen plugs carried the defect. A linear scan has no ordering invariant to get wrong and this runs once per call site at transpile time.

author: blu
body: This list was wrapped in a sort helper that was the IDENTITY function (sort-go-builtins (xs) = xs), which is worse than no sort at all: the list read as though something ordered it at startup, so the binary search over it looked justified, and two audits of this defect missed this plug because of it. The stub is deleted. If a sort is ever reintroduced here it must actually sort, by the same comparator the lookup uses.
